author: Richard Driehaus
note: The momentum pioneer's famous line. Strength tends to persist longer than most investors expect.

quote: Stocks are never too high for you to begin buying or too low to begin selling.
author: Jesse Livermore, Reminiscences of a Stock Operator
note: Price levels alone mean little. Direction and strength matter more.

author: Martin Zweig
note: When the market's trend is clear, working against it is expensive. Rules help you go with it.

quote: My metric for everything I look at is the 200-day moving average of closing prices.
author: Paul Tudor Jones
note: A simple trend filter keeps you on the right side of big moves and out of long declines.

quote: The trend is your friend except at the end when it bends.
author: Ed Seykota
note: Follow trends, but always have an exit rule for when they turn.

quote: Cut your losses short and let your profits run.
author: Trading maxim (often credited to David Ricardo)
note: The heart of every momentum system: small losses, big winners.

author: Eugene Fama (attributed)
note: Even the father of efficient markets has acknowledged how hard momentum is to explain away.

quote: It never was my thinking that made the big money for me. It always was my sitting.
author: Jesse Livermore
note: Momentum rewards holding winners. Most investors sell them far too early.

quote: Markets can remain in a trend far longer than seems reasonable.
author: Trend-following principle
note: Trends don't end because they look 'too far'. Let the rules, not your opinion, decide the exit.

quote: Plan your trade and trade your plan.
author: Trading maxim
note: A momentum system only works if every rebalance follows the same rules.

quote: You don't need to know what is going to happen next in order to make money.
author: Mark Douglas
note: Systematic momentum doesn't predict. It reacts to what prices are already doing.

author: Paul Tudor Jones
note: Momentum adds to strength and exits weakness, the opposite of averaging down.
